key_points.point: The document emphasizes that AI is a transformative tool that amplifies human potential, and the primary challenge for leaders is to move beyond experimentation to integrate AI at scale to capture its full value.
key_points.verbatim: Each era’s boldest breakthroughs—from harnessing steam to building the internet—began when people leveraged new tools to amplify their potential. Artificial intelligence (AI) is the latest chapter in this story.

key_points.point: The report highlights that AI is already delivering measurable productivity and efficiency gains across enterprises, which serves as a foundation for further transformation.
key_points.verbatim: AI is already boosting productivity and efficiency; just a subset are using it to rewrite the business.

key_points.point: The document argues for a pragmatic approach where leaders focus on practical steps to integrate AI into core processes, viewing AI as a force multiplier for human expertise.
key_points.verbatim: Business leaders today face an unprecedented challenge: moving beyond pilots to truly integrating AI into the heart of their organizations. It requires a deliberate shift in which people set a vision and make responsible choices, and AI provides the insights, speed, and scale to deliver against that ambition.

key_points.point: The document advocates for a model where AI and human strengths—judgment, creativity, empathy—are combined to elevate organizational performance rather than simply automating tasks.
key_points.verbatim: That means redesigning core processes and operating models with AI, ensuring that human strengths—such as judgment, creativity, empathy, and relationship-building—are elevated, not automated.

key_points.point: The report encourages leaders to be visionary and pursue strategic reinvention, suggesting that AI allows for business models and workflows that were previously impossible.
key_points.verbatim: Now is the time to be visionary—reshaping organizational structures, roles, and workflows in ways that may not have been possible before.

key_points.point: The document warns that the rapid deployment of autonomous AI agents is outpacing the development of necessary governance and oversight guardrails.
key_points.verbatim: Autonomous AI agents are racing into the enterprise, but oversight is lagging. Nearly 3 in 4 (74%) companies plan to deploy agentic AI within two years. Yet, 1 in 5 (21%) report having a mature model for governance of autonomous agents, raising the specter of unintended risks.

key_points.point: The report notes that physical AI systems interact with the real world in ways that pose safety risks if they malfunction, necessitating rigorous testing and certification.
key_points.verbatim: Unlike software AI that operates in digital environments, physical AI systems interact with people, equipment, and infrastructure in ways that can pose safety risks if they malfunction or are compromised. This raises the stakes for testing, certification, and ongoing monitoring.

key_points.point: The document highlights that governance is a critical prerequisite for scaling, and organizations that fail to build it early will likely stall in their AI efforts.
key_points.verbatim: In the AI era, governance is more than guardrails—it’s the catalyst for responsible growth. Enterprises where senior leadership actively shapes AI governance achieve significantly greater business value than those delegating the work to technical teams alone.
key_points.excerpt_context: Key findings, A closer look at governance

key_points.point: The report emphasizes the need for clear boundaries and audit trails for autonomous agents to ensure accountability and manage the risks of independent action.
key_points.verbatim: Organizations need to establish clear boundaries for agent autonomy, defining which decisions agents can make independently versus which require human approval. Real-time monitoring systems that track agent behavior and flag anomalies are essential, as are audit trails that capture the full chain of agent actions to help ensure accountability and enable continuous improvement.
key_points.excerpt_context: Key findings, Managing the risks of agentic AI

key_points.point: The document identifies that the complexity of AI supply chains and the lack of visibility into production environments create significant security and compliance risks.
key_points.verbatim: In some organizations, leaders are learning AI models have been deployed into production without formal oversight or monitoring processes. In particular, one AI leader discovered that there wasn’t a clear inventory of all the AI tools and models currently active because development efforts occurred without systematic tracking or centralized visibility over what is running in production.
key_points.excerpt_context: Key findings, A closer look at governance

key_points.point: The document acknowledges that while AI is expected to automate jobs, most companies have not yet redesigned work or talent strategies to support the affected workforce.
key_points.verbatim: Despite high expectations for automation, 84% of companies have not redesigned jobs or the nature of work itself around AI capabilities. Insufficient worker skills are seen as the biggest barrier to integrating AI into the business, but fewer than half of companies are making significant adjustments to their talent strategies.

key_points.point: The report notes that while access to AI tools has increased, actual daily usage by workers remains low, suggesting that the promised productivity gains are not being realized as expected.
key_points.verbatim: While access is widening, enterprise AI remains underutilized, and its productivity and innovation potential are still largely untapped.
key_points.excerpt_context: Key findings, AI is moving from the pilot and experimentation phase

key_points.point: The document points out that many AI pilot projects fail to scale because organizations lack the necessary infrastructure, integration, and strategic planning, leading to 'pilot fatigue.'
key_points.verbatim: Without a clear roadmap, executing a hundred pilots just leads to poor results and failed value creation.

key_points.point: The report highlights that the costs of physical AI deployment, including infrastructure and facility modifications, are often underestimated, leading to project failures.
key_points.verbatim: Companies that underestimate these costs risk project delays or abandonment partway through implementation.
key_points.excerpt_context: Key findings, Accounting for the full cost of physical AI

key_points.point: The document warns that organizations are struggling to modernize their technical infrastructure and data management, which remains a persistent barrier to AI adoption.
key_points.verbatim: Perceptions of preparedness shifted down slightly for technical infrastructure, data management and talent, revealing the persistent challenge of modernizing systems and skills at the speed of innovation.

factual_claims.claim: Worker access to sanctioned AI tools has increased by 50% in one year, growing from under 40% to nearly 60% of the workforce.
Only 25% of surveyed organizations have moved 40% or more of their AI experiments into production to date.
77% of companies consider the geographic location of AI development a key factor when selecting new AI technologies.
74% of companies plan to deploy agentic AI within the next two years.
58% of companies are currently using physical AI, with adoption expected to reach 80% within two years.
